notes: digestVectors: body is the task-start attestation body (v2, 14 keys). expected.ok = digest and the exact preimage bytes (UTF8 domain albera.task-start-attestation.v2, 0x00, canonical map as in action-digest.mjs); otherwise expected.code (malformed | ttl) and field.

actionDigest (issue #133) is the "sha256:" action digest of the guest.command DTO the Authority will sign for the task start; the Authority computes it itself and the verifier compares it, so one statement backs exactly one action. The two digests used here are the action digests of {action: task.start, projectId: proj-alpha, computerId: pc-01, args: {expectedGeneration: 3, task: "build the project" | "delete everything", vmId: 11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555}}.
The C# twin is TaskStartAttestation.cs (digest vectors and verifyVectors). It reproduces every expected value here in the dotnet contract test.

verifyVectors: the public half of an EPHEMERAL ECDSA P-256 test key (publicKeySpki, base64 DER; the private key was discarded after signing, nothing secret is in this file) and signed envelopes made with it. For each case, verifyTaskStartAttestation(signed, { clock: now, verify: the pinned key under keyId, expected }) must give result: ok, or the code and field of the refusal. The signature is ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256 over the canonical bytes, IEEE P1363 (64 bytes), unpadded base64url. Both the Node and C# implementations must reproduce every result.

A statement with network "present" / "unknown" or checkpointType "standard" verifies here (ok): whether it is ENOUGH is the Authority's rule (network none AND checkpointType production), not the verifier's.

invalid_expected cases: the caller's own expected values are checked before the statement is read, and named in a fixed order (computerId, projectId, leaseId, operationId, vmId, actionDigest, generation, leaseGeneration); the two counters must be safe integers (at most 9007199254740991), in both twins.
Bindings are reported in the order actionDigest, computerId, generation, leaseGeneration, leaseId, operationId, projectId, vmId.

The last cases pin domain separation: a genuine network attestation (10-key body, network domain) is malformed here, a genuine statement of the previous version (13 keys, v1 domain, no actionDigest) is malformed here, and a task-start body signed or digested under the network domain does not verify.
